title: Camshaft Position Actuator Circuit / Open (Bank 1)
shortDescription: Variable valve timing actuator A on bank 1 has an open circuit fault.
fullDescription: Variable valve timing actuator A on bank 1 has an open circuit fault.
safetyImpact: Engine timing faults can cause stalling and reduce control authority during driving.

causes.cause: Low or dirty engine oil restricting solenoid flow
Stretched timing chain or worn tensioner
Wiring or connector issue at solenoid

fixSteps.title: Check oil level and quality
fixSteps.instruction: Verify engine oil is at the correct level and not overdue. VVT systems are highly sensitive to oil condition; change with manufacturer-spec oil if needed.

fixSteps.title: Read freeze frame and live data
fixSteps.instruction: Use a scanner with VVT data PIDs to compare commanded vs actual cam timing during a road test.

fixSteps.title: Test VVT solenoid
fixSteps.instruction: Remove the OCV solenoid, inspect the screen for debris, and test resistance against specification. Apply 12 V to verify it clicks open and closed.

fixSteps.title: Inspect timing chain and phaser
fixSteps.instruction: If solenoid and oil are good, inspect timing chain stretch and cam phaser operation. Replacement requires front cover removal.

faq.q: Will the wrong oil cause VVT codes?
faq.a: Yes. Using oil that is too thick, too thin, or overdue for change is one of the most common causes of VVT solenoid faults.

faq.q: Is it safe to drive with a VVT code?
faq.a: Short trips at light load are usually safe, but prolonged driving with a stuck phaser can cause cam chain wear and major engine damage.

faq.q: How much does VVT solenoid replacement cost?
faq.a: The solenoid itself is typically $30-$120, with $100-$300 labor. Phaser or chain replacement can exceed $1,500.
